extractedText: AI That Guarded Factories Now Guards Public Safety■2026 Ulsan Forum AI Applied to Traditional Markets to Prevent Fires Vision AI in Ambulances Secures the Golden Hour "AI That Protected Industrial Equipment Now Protects Citizens"Finance|Published 2026.09.13. 08:00:05|By Jang Hyun-kilucky@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAFrom left: Lee Soon-yeol, CEO of Qnesty; Yoon Hye-jin, vice president of IT Space; Je Young-jun, head of the startup division at the Ulsan Center for Creative Economy and Innovation; Kim Ji-hoon, CEO of Dolbomdream; and Park Si-eun, CEO of Dalgu, discuss ways to apply artificial intelligence in everyday life at the 2026 Ulsan Forum held at the Ulsan Exhibition and Convention Center (UECO) on Nov. 11. Photo by Jang Hyun-kiArtificial intelligence that once detected equipment defects and prevented accidents at industrial sites is expanding into everyday life, from traditional markets and elderly care facilities to the inside of ambulances.At the 2026 Ulsan Forum, hosted by SK on the 11th at the Ulsan Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the Ulsan Exhibition & Convention Center (UECO), officials from social innovation companies shared a range of cases in which AI is being used in daily life.One case presented at the forum involved a smart electrical fire safety system installed at traditional markets in Incheon, which reduced the rate of major fires. The project became possible when ITSpace, a social innovation company, applied UYeG, a current-based predictive maintenance AI it had used at industrial sites, to the markets. UYeG gives advance warning of abnormalities in current, temperature and arcing, helping prevent related accidents. Yoon Hye-jin, vice president of ITSpace, said the project cut the rate of electrical fires at traditional markets by 60% and reduced maintenance costs by 40%.Another presentation covered a care safety net reflecting the country's aging population. Kim Ji-hoon, chief executive of Dolbomdream, introduced Caerly, which monitors heart rate, respiration and sleep data of older adults using an air-pressure-based ballistocardiography (BCG) sensor. A BCG sensor is a non-invasive device that measures the minute vibrations generated in the body by heartbeats. Caerly detects health abnormalities in older adults through the sensor, and AI analyzes the data to give early warning of conditions such as arrhythmia and heart failure. The system deploys AI instead of additional staff to assist those in need of health monitoring.Park Si-eun, chief executive of Dalgu, proposed ways to resolve information gaps in emergency medical care using AI. Dalgu, a digital healthcare company, is developing technology that shares the vital signs of patients being transported by ambulance with hospitals in real time and analyzes first-aid procedures using vision AI. The approach uses AI to overcome the limits of a system in which ambulance transport information depends on radio and phone calls, securing the golden hour.Industry officials said AI, once used mainly for factory management, is widening its scope to protect public safety. Yoon said, "AI that has protected equipment at industrial sites is now moving toward becoming AI that protects the safety of citizens in our cities." Je Young-jun, head of the startup division at the Ulsan Center for Creative Economy & Innovation, added, "There is a lot of room to move technology proven at industrial sites into areas that citizens can feel directly."#UlsanForum#AI#PublicSafety#SmartCity#DigitalHealthcare#PredictiveMaintenanceOriginal reporting by Jang Hyun-ki for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
